title: Tenant-aware warm scheduling and adaptive prewarm budget for dedicated fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a tenant-aware warm scheduler and an adaptive prewarm budget controller for Dedicated fleets to reduce cold-start latency while preserving throughput guarantees and memory headroom. This work coordinates weight residency, KV hydration, and a budget-driven eviction window so that model instances brought up for reserved customers achieve target P50/P95 cold-starts without dramatically increasing tail memory usage or blocking autoscaler decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Average cold-start P95 (first token latency after allocation) for reserved tenants <= 220ms across synthetic workload A
End-to-end throughput for a warmed fleet meets committed throughput targets under standard burst profile (95th percentile within 5% of baseline)
KV hydration cost (extra token-equivalent CPU/GPU) per warmup kept under configured budget per-tenant
No more than 3% increase in OOM/eviction incidents in production after rollout
notes: Design focuses on a two-stage warm: 1) weight locality reservation (fast memcpy or partial load), 2) KV hydration using fingerprinted prefix cache + lazy backbone hydration
We will expose a per-tenant prewarm_budget parameter (tokens-equivalent) and an autoscaler hint that can be used to throttle warm concurrency

Trade-offs discussed: aggressive preloading reduces latency but raises memory residency and can starve capacity for other tenants. Conservative approach uses fingerprinted KV and progressive hydration windows.
Operational signals: use cold-start-trace span, weight-load-duration histogram, kv-hydration-bytes, warm-budget-consumed; hook into console rollout gating

implementation_notes: Scheduler will tag allocations with tenant-warm-status and warm_budget_reserved metadata to ensure fair eviction decisions
KV hydration will use a fingerprint to decide prioritized prefix hydration. Full KV loads only after soft-SLOs are met
Autoscaler integration: expose warm_request_hint to the cluster autoscaler so scale-up accounts for warm concurrency without violating throughput SLAs
Fallback: if warm-budget exhausted, fall back to cold-start-safe mode that prioritizes throughput over latency (smaller batch sizes, no prefetch)
qa_plan: Create synthetic tenants with varied model sizes (1.8B, 7B, 13B) and run burst patterns from 1->100 QPS
Measure P50/P95 cold-start latency, throughput, memory residency and eviction rates across canary clusters
Run chaos tests that force simultaneous warm events to validate global concurrency cap and backpressure
